title: travel-digest-llm-systems-sketches
content:
Short travel digest + reading notes from SIGSYS week (lightweight, messy)

Context: flew to SF for 3 days of talks and partner syncs. Pulled together quick reads while between sessions; this is my personal scratchpad — half summary, half experiment sketch.

1) FlashAttention-2 / memory-efficient attention notes (session + paper skim)
- Core claim: better memory locality + kernel fusion; lower mem overhead for long sequences.
- Useful for Redwood serving runtime if we can reduce KV-cache footprint per-shard.
- Quick takeaway: measure live latencies on 8k / 16k sequences with 8-bit kernels; focus on max batch size that keeps p95 < 120ms.
- Experiment idea: swap kernel in nightly serving canary for one small-model shard, run A/B for 24h with synthetic trace replay. Metric: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU mem headroom.
- Open question: stability with quantized weights (4/3-bit). Does FA2 tolerate weight rounding? Add to test matrix.

2) KV-MoE (Mixture-of-Experts for KV routing) — notes from poster + hallway convo
- Intuition: route context spans to specialized KV experts (hot prefixes -> cached experts). Could reduce average KV mem by factor of active-expert fraction.
- Practical constraints: routing table size, offload overhead, load imbalance.
- Quick sketch: maintain LRU of active kv-experts per-customer, shard experts by prefix hash. Fallback to dense KV for cold prefixes.
- Risks: tail latency spikes when hot-expert fails; need graceful fallback policy (route to smaller model variant).

3) RAG + on-device reranking talk — field notes
- Speaker: research lead at partner startup; emphasized reranker cost dominates retrieval stack for low-cost production apps.
- Idea: two-stage rerank: cheap lexical filter -> small distilled cross-encoder -> full cross-encoder only top-K. Apply same principle to prompt-level reranking inside a single request chain to save tokens.
- Application for Redwood: suggest to product team a cookbook for multi-stage reranking with budget targets (p50 < 200ms, cost reduction > 30%).

4) Lightweight evals & drift detection (panel notes)
- Keep small representative prompt sets per-customer (50–200 prompts) to watch quality regressions after model/quant changes.
- Proposal: integrate per-route baseline prompts in Console (opt-in), run nightly A/B and surface divergence alerts.
- Implementation note: include synthetic noise to surface brittle behaviors.

5) Personal experiment backlog (concrete steps)
- EX-1: FlashAttention kernel canary
  - Checkout: example-repo:feature/flash-canary (PR linked above).
  - Steps: deploy canary to dedicated pool (2 GPUs), enable 1% traffic for route /v1/generate/canary, run 72h replay.
  - Success: no >1% increase in error rate, p95 latency within 10% of baseline, GPU mem reduction >= 12%.

- EX-2: KV-expert LRU prototype (mini)
  - Dataset: internal prefix-trace.json (sample of 10k sessions).
  - Metric: average KV storage per-session, tail latency when evicting experts.
  - Implementation note: implement eviction hook to write-to-SSD (fast local NVMe) and measure write/read penalty.

- EX-3: Multi-stage reranker guide for customers (doc draft)
  - Deliverable: 1-pager + example notebook (python) showing retrieval -> distilled reranker -> full reranker.
  - Goal: reduce rerank token cost by 40% for FAQ-style retrieval apps.

6) Snippets from papers I want to read deeper (to triage later)
- "Sparse KV as a service" (TODO: read full paper, highlight costs).
- "Quantization-aware attention" (check evaluation on 4-bit models).
- "Adaptive batching for short-tail latency" (interesting for bursty APIs).

7) Meeting TODOs and followups
- Ping Samir for prefix-trace location and sample format. (Samir: slack me the path)
- Add EX-1 to canary calendar (Ops + SRE review) — assign JIRA-ENG-3421.
- Draft reranker 1-pager and circulate to Solutions Eng by next Tue.
- Ask Product-hosted-api about telemetry hooks for nightly A/B datasets.

8) Quick heuristics / quick wins observed at conference
- Always run a tiny synthetic workload (50 req/s of typical short prompts) after kernel change to surface early regressions.
- Keep a tiny labelled eval set per major customer — makes rollback decisions faster.
- For talks: prioritize reproducible benchmarks (raw logs + seeds) over single-run numbers.

Random notes (scattershot):
- Meeting with partner ops: they'd accept a small library that converts their trace -> rps-replay format (I should sketch converter).
- Senior researcher suggested a thesis: "cache-aware quantization" where quantization profile depends on prefix reuse probability — sounds promising.
- My gut: start with FlashAttention canary before larger KV experiments. Lower blast radius.

Questions for the group (to put in weekly sync):
- Are we comfortable exposing per-route baseline prompt sets in Console as opt-in (privacy considerations)?
- What are SRE concerns for ephemeral on-disk KV offload?

End of quick travel/digest scratchpad.

-- Noor
(quick, messy; will expand into PRD + playbook if one of the experiments looks promising)
